text: Chapter 3 moves from formatted statements to ad hoc exploration: Oracle Transactional Business Intelligence, OTBI. Before building anything, you need one concept: subject areas.

OTBI analyzes live transactional data, not a pre-summarized cube refreshed on a schedule. It queries the exact current state of Payables invoices or GL journals right now. That makes it the right tool for "what does this look like at this exact moment," a different question from what a formatted monthly statement shows.

You don't write SQL against OTBI. Oracle curates subject areas, business-friendly groupings of facts, the measures you total like invoice amount or days overdue, and dimensions, the attributes you slice by, like business unit, customer, or supplier. Building an analysis means picking facts and dimensions out of a subject area and letting OTBI assemble the query.

Financial subject areas are organized per product: Assets, Budgetary Control, Cash Management, Expenses, General Ledger, Intercompany, Payables, Receivables, Revenue Management, Subledger Accounting. The Payables subject area gives you invoice-level facts and dimensions; it won't give you Fixed Assets data, because that lives in its own subject area. And a user's duty roles determine which subject areas even show up for them.

Under the hood, OTBI runs real-time queries against the application's own data, which is exactly why it can show an invoice entered thirty seconds ago, where a cube-based report can't. Up next, lesson eleven: building your first OTBI analysis.
